themes_detail.label: Tree Deaths Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying trees complaints surged to 8 THIS WEEK versus 1.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 482% spike (z-score: 13.68)—suggesting rapid environmental degradation or disease affecting the district's canopy this week.
evidence: 8 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Aligns with CB budget requests for park/amenity upgrades (recurring ask suggesting chronic tree maintenance gaps)
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about cause of cluster—disease outbreak, pest infestation, or deferred maintenance?
Map specific locations and identify if complaints cluster in one neighborhood section or spread across Bensonhurst/Bath Beach

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Clogging Streets
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 23 THIS WEEK, up 159% from the 8.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.81), indicating an accelerating abandoned-car problem affecting parking and street safety this week.
evidence: 23 derelict vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.9 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Compounds illegal parking (6,587 complaints over 90 days, the district's highest complaint category)
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and Sanitation about removal capacity—are they overwhelmed or is the inflow accelerating?
Identify specific streets or blocks with clusters of abandoned cars; talk to residents about blocking driveways and parking access

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness-related encampment complaints exploded to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.1 weekly average—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—indicating an emerging or newly visible homeless encampment crisis in the district this week.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Aligns with CB budget requests for mental health de-stigmatization and outreach services to vulnerable populations
reporting_angles: Locate specific encampment sites and assess size, duration, and services available or needed
Interview residents, encampment occupants, and NYC Department of Homeless Services about whether this is a new trend or newly reported issue

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Discoveries in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints hit 11 LAST WEEK, up 1,367% from the 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 12.36)—a sharp spike suggesting either recent construction/demolition activity (514 DOB filings in 90 days including 10 full demolitions) or newly discovered contamination requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 11 asbestos complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (8-week baseline)
514 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (417 alterations, 10 full demolitions) creating potential disturbance and exposure risk
reporting_angles: Cross-reference asbestos complaints with DOB demolition and alteration permits to see if spike correlates with construction activity
Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection and Buildings about enforcement of asbestos abatement rules during demolitions

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Outbreak Signal
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 700% from the 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)—a pattern that may indicate a foodborne illness cluster or contaminated restaurant that warrants immediate public health follow-up.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Cluster suggests possible common source (restaurant or food vendor) rather than random incidents
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to determine if they identified a common restaurant or food source and what enforcement action was taken
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timeline, and where they ate in days preceding illness
